scenes.title: SQL Syntax
scenes.narration: SQL syntax is the set of rules that shapes every valid statement, and knowing it keeps your queries readable and correct.

scenes.title: Building blocks
bullets: Keywords like SELECT and FROM drive the command
Identifiers name your tables and columns
Clauses appear in a fixed, expected order
scenes.narration: Keywords such as SELECT and FROM are reserved words that tell the database what action to perform. Identifiers are the names you give to tables and columns, and they must match what exists in the schema. Clauses follow a fixed order so the parser can interpret each statement consistently.

scenes.title: Anatomy of a statement
scenes.narration: Every statement begins with a command keyword that sets its purpose. You then list the columns or values involved and name the target table. Optional clauses refine the result, and a semicolon marks the end of the statement.

scenes.title: Readable formatting
scenes.narration: Notice how each clause sits on its own line for readability. SELECT and FROM are uppercase keywords, while the lowercase names are identifiers pointing at real columns and a table. The WHERE clause filters the rows, and the semicolon cleanly closes the statement.

scenes.text: Consistent syntax and clean formatting make SQL easy to read, review, and debug across any team.
scenes.narration: Following consistent syntax rules and formatting your clauses cleanly makes queries far easier to read and maintain.
